gauge_shift_definition.what: Crust header (mn,mp) is shifted to the CORE's header (mn,mp); Q3/Q4/Q6/Q7 are re-derived so physical F/mu_B/mu_Q are INVARIANT; Q1 (P/n_B), Q2, Q5, Iphase, composition, n_B grid unchanged. The CORE is kept at its ORIGINAL gauge (no Q re-derivation).
gauge_shift_definition.dmcr: dmcr = core_mn - crust_mn, applied to the crust F/mu_B (mirrors match_crust_core compose_eos_matching.f90:539); here promoted to a full mn/mp header unification so the v1 Maxwell mass gate (compose_eos_phase_transition.f90:689) passes.
gauge_shift_definition.NOT_PDG_regeneration: PDG regeneration (matched_pdg_gauge_v2, commit eeca35c) rewrites BOTH phases to PDG mn/mp. Gauge shift rewrites ONLY the crust to the core's gauge; the core is untouched. The Q-value algebra is identical (ratio = mn_src/mn_tgt), but the target mn differs: PDG (939.56542052) vs the pair's core mn.

physics_proof_why_stability_gate_is_inva.claim: A constant gauge shift of mu_B (header mn unification + Q re-derivation) leaves the n(mu) curve SHAPE and dn/dmu invariant.
physics_proof_why_stability_gate_is_inva.reason: validate_phase builds mu_grid = (eps + P)/nb. The header-mn shift changes eps (and hence mu_grid) by a CONSTANT nb*dmcr per point, so d(mu)/d(nb) -- the quantity the Hermite interpolant's n(mu) depends on -- is unchanged (d(const)/dnb = 0). The quadratic-vertex stability test (n>0, dn/dmu>0) is identical before and after the shift. Therefore the crust segment Hermite artifact (SPG_M1 Iphase 7 interval 0: dn/dmu = -4.79e-3 at t=0.531, mu=941.136 MeV) is reproduced IDENTICALLY under the gauge shift.

gauge_shift_this_run.note: Header mn/mp unified (crust shifted to core gauge, core original); mass gate passes. The stability gate fails identically to the PDG-regeneration run because the n(mu) curve shape is gauge-invariant.

pdg_regen_commit_eeca35c.note: Both phases rewritten to PDG mn/mp. Mass gate passes. Stability gate fails identically (same n(mu) shape).

gauge_shift_vs_pdg_regen_comparison.conclusion: A gauge shift is NOT a viable path to a v2 Maxwell matched EOS for these sources. It passes the mass gate (header unification) but leaves the crust segment Hermite stability artifact untouched (gauge-invariant n(mu) curve). The empirical gate distributions of the two strategies are statistically indistinguishable: both reject all 65 pairs at the physics (stability/coexistence) gate, NOT at the mass-convention gate. The mass-convention problem was solved by EITHER strategy; the crust segment interpolation-quality problem is independent of gauge convention and requires smooth interpolation preprocessing (M5 smooth-matrix scope), not a gauge transformation.

deliverable.reason: No (crust, core) pair passes the validate_phase Hermite stability gate under a gauge shift, so no matched EOS table is exported. The manifest is the sole deliverable for this review; it documents the gauge-shift attempt, the physics proof of gate invariance, and the 65-pair gate distribution.
deliverable.distinct_from_pdg_regeneration_run: This run is kept in download/matched_gauge_shift_v2/ (separate from download/matched_pdg_gauge_v2/) and labeled method= 'maxwell_v2_gauge_shift' so any future survivor would never be confused with a PDG-regeneration table.
